title: Shadow traffic broker with tenant slab accounting and proportional sampling
creator: Samira Patel
description: Goal: implement a production-ready shadow traffic broker that safely duplicates a subset of live requests to candidate model variants while enforcing per-tenant cost slabs, strong isolation, and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a broker service (stateless control plane + per-node state) that maintains tenant slabs and admission logic; 2) a proportional/stratified sampling engine that adapts sampling probability based on each tenant's remaining slab and observed budget burn rate; 3) a sandboxed execution path for mirrored requests (sidecar isolation + non-producing metrics) to avoid customer-facing regressions; 4) integration points with the rollout controller for auto-rollback when shadow-driven metrics regress beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Broker can accept production traffic and replicate it to a shadow cluster at a configurable global sampling rate. 2) Per-tenant slabs (monthly token credits) limit total mirrored token volume; slabs are decremented in near-real-time and prevent overspend. 3) Sampling adapts per-tenant: if slab burn is accelerating, sampling decays smoothly (exponential backoff of p with guard rails). 4) Mirrored requests execute with strict isolation: no writes to stateful downstreams, no side-effects, and are tagged so they never affect billing. 5) Rollout controller receives shadow metrics (latency, error, n-gram quality regressions) and can trigger an automated halt+rollback if thresholds exceeded. 6) End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios demonstrating tenant quarantine, over-burn recovery, and rollback fire are in CI.
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Shadow+Broker+Design (internal). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/shadow-broker/pull/62. Load/perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/shadow-broker/production. Background: existing mirror solutions either over-allocate cost or provide coarse tenant-level throttles. This design targets predictable economics using small, per-tenant reservoirs and proportional sampling. Key metrics: mirrored_tokens, slab_remaining, p_sampling_current, mirrored_latency_p50/p95, mirrored_error_rate, quality_delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics for targeted prompts).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement broker control plane + per-node in-memory slab cache, API to top-up slabs, and config for global/tenant sampling. Phase 2 (week 3): implement proportional sampling algorithm + safety gate that prevents sampling below minimum p_min. Phase 3 (week 4): integrate sandboxed sidecar runner and ensure mirrored requests are tagged and write-protected. Phase 4 (week 5): hook into rollout controller for metrics ingestion and automated rollback policies; add alerting. Phase 5 (week 6): run canary across 10 tenants then expand; add performance tuning and telemetry. Rollout will be gated behind a feature flag with an emergency kill switch.
design_decisions: - Use a per-tenant slab model (token-based) rather than pure quota-percentage to give finance predictable chargebacks. - Sampling algorithm: stratified proportional sampler (tenant p = min(p_global * slab_remaining_ratio, p_max)). This reduces sampling smoothly as slab depletes. - Implement local lease-backed slab caches (refresh interval 5s) to avoid hot-disk contention on the authoritative slab store. - Sidecars run mirrored inference in sandbox mode with strict env vars preventing network egress and with a read-only flag for downstream connectors. - Mirror requests are not counted as billable usage in the billing pipeline; separate accounting event streams are emitted for internal cost reports.
tradeoffs: - Consistency vs cost: local slab caches reduce latency at the cost of short-lived overshoot (bounded by lease TTL). Mitigation: conservative decrement and write-through reconciliations. - Sampling accuracy vs stability: a rapid p adjustment reacts quickly to overburn but can produce oscillation; we prefer a smoothed EWMA of burn-rate with momentum to stabilize p. - Isolation complexity: sandboxed sidecars add operational overhead and resource footprint; but they greatly reduce risk of mirrored side-effects. - Observability load: emitting full mirrored traces increases telemetry costs; we sample telemetry at a lower rate and emit summary metrics for every request.
risks: 1) Tenant slab desync leading to brief overbilling or undersampling; risk lowered via periodic reconciliation and conservative buffering. 2) Performance impact on gateways when enabling replication for large tenants; mitigated with backpressure and per-tenant caps. 3) Regression detection false positives causing unnecessary rollbacks; addressed by multi-metric heuristics and temporarily requiring persistence across multiple windows before auto-rollback.
tests_and_validation: - Unit tests for sampler math and slab accounting. - Integration tests: mocked slab store + broker + sandbox runner executing mirrored sequences. - Load test: 100k req/s synthetic traffic with 500 tenants to measure latency tail and slab contention. - Chaos test: simulate slab-store partition and ensure graceful degraded mode (sampling disabled for affected tenants and they are quarantined). - Regression experiments: inject small model changes in shadow and verify rollout controller flags quality delta > 2% and triggers auto-halt in canary group.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal testbed (non-prod) with synthetic tenants for 1 week. 2) Alpha: enable for 10 low-volume production tenants behind opt-in flag. 3) Beta: expand to 100 tenants with financial owners notified. 4) GA: open to all tenants after two weeks of stable ops and SLO attainment. Emergency rollback: feature-flag kill + distributed kill-switch that drains in-flight mirrored requests and instructs rollout controller to pause all shadowing.
required_reviews: - Security: sandbox sidecar execution model (requested). - Finance: per-tenant slab accounting semantics. - Product: rollout thresholds and customer-facing opt-in copy. - SRE: paging thresholds for mirrored pipeline degradation. Reviewers: Alex Martinez (Security), Priya Nambiar (Finance), Marco Ruiz (SRE), Nina Goldberg (Product).
outstanding_questions: 1) Should mirrored telemetry be retained at full fidelity or downsampled for cost? Proposal: downsample traces, but emit full aggregated metrics per request. 2) How to expose slab top-ups to customers: UI in Console vs API-only. 3) Should we provide 'grace credits' for low-volume tenants to avoid immediate quarantine? (prefers yes for trial experience).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Samira Patel: Initial draft of the slab-based broker is implemented in the prototype repo. Basic API for top-up and slab-query added. Need feedback on lease TTL tradeoffs.

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented stratified proportional sampler. Observed oscillation when burn spikes; switched to EWMA smoothing with alpha=0.25. Added unit tests covering edge cases (slab==0, p_min enforcement).

2026-03-06 - Priya Nambiar (Finance): Reviewed slab semantics. Requested an audit log event for every slab top-up and monthly export for chargeback. Also requested a default free trial slab of 1M tokens for new tenants.

2026-03-07 - Alex Martinez (Security): Sandbox sidecar model acceptable but requires egress-block rules + HSM keys not mounted in sandbox. Requested a short threat model doc and runtime attestation checks.
2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Load test plan added. Concern: gateway's CPU can spike when mirroring large responses; proposing CPU-based backpressure along with token-based slab checks.

2026-03-11 - Nina Goldberg (Product): Agreed on default rollout thresholds: quality_delta > 3% sustained for 3 windows OR mirrored_error_rate increase > 1.5x triggers auto-halt. Product requested a Console toggle to view per-tenant slab status.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Open PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/shadow-broker/pull/79 with initial broker + sampler. Running internal canary tomorrow with 5 tenants.
